facts.value: No state final-pay statute; wages are due by the regular payday for the last pay period
facts.summary: Florida has no state final-pay statute; federal law does not require an immediate final check, so final wages are due on the regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Employers are not required by federal law to give former employees their final paycheck immediately. Some states, however, may require immediate payment.
facts.notes: Basis: absence of statute. The official 2026 Florida Statutes Chapter 448 Part I section list (https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/Chapter448/Part_I) has no final-pay timing section; the only unpaid-wage section is 448.08 (attorney's fees). U.S. DOL payday table footnote 1: Florida, no regulations. No Florida agency page states this outright.

facts.summary: Florida basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00 The Florida minimum wage is scheduled to be updated annually based on a set formula beginning January 1, 2028.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.
